content.value_statement: Teams often apply Next.js App Router patterns inconsistently. This skill gives concise guidance for pages, layouts, routing, data fetching, fonts, and metadata.
actual_capabilities: Explains where App Router pages and layouts belong.
Guides when to use Server Components or Client Components.
Shows internal navigation with Link and useRouter.
Describes server and client data fetching choices.
Covers next/font usage and metadata placement.
limitations: Does not include automated lint rules or tests.
Does not cover API routes, middleware, or deployment settings.
Does not provide detailed Server Actions examples.
Assumes a project already uses the Next.js App Router.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Route
use_cases.description: Choose page and layout locations before adding a new App Router route.

use_cases.title: Review Component Boundaries
use_cases.description: Decide whether a component should stay server-side or require client behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Guidance
use_cases.description: Give a team short rules for routing, fonts, metadata, and data fetching.

prompt_templates.title: Locate a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a new Next.js App Router page. Tell me the correct page file location and any layout considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Component Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component idea. Tell me whether it should be a Server Component or Client Component, and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Navigation and Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: For this feature, recommend the navigation method and data fetching approach using the project Next.js patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review an App Router Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js App Router feature plan. Recommend file locations, component boundaries, navigation approach, data fetching, font usage, and metadata.

output_examples.input: Add a dashboard page with internal navigation.
output_examples.output: Use an App Router page under the dashboard route. Use Link for internal navigation and keep stateful navigation in a Client Component.

output_examples.input: Decide how a settings page should fetch profile data.
output_examples.output: Fetch data in a Server Component when possible. Use client fetching only when browser state or live client updates are required.

output_examples.input: Set up project typography and search metadata.
output_examples.output: Load fonts through next/font in the root layout. Place metadata exports in the relevant page or layout for SEO.

best_practices: Default to Server Components unless state, effects, or browser APIs are required.
Use Link for internal navigation and useRouter only inside Client Components.
Define metadata close to the page or layout that owns the SEO context.
anti_patterns: Do not mark every component with use client by default.
Do not use programmatic routing when a normal Link is sufficient.
Do not scatter font setup across many components.

faq.question: Does this skill write Next.js code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and review guidance. It does not include scripts or generated files.

faq.question: Does it support the App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on the Next.js 15 App Router under the app directory.

faq.question: Does it cover Client Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when the use client directive is appropriate for state, effects, and browser APIs.

faq.question: Does it cover routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Link for internal navigation and useRouter for programmatic client navigation.

faq.question: Does it include data fetching guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends server fetching where possible and client fetching for client-side needs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
